clue.text: Top of the bill at Carnegie Hall? (Margate's quite wrong!)

definitions.text: Top of the bill at Carnegie Hall?

indicators.note: letters that are quite wrong are in the wrong order and must be set right

blocks.note: the seaside town with its possessive S, all eight letters used

explanation.surface: An exclamation contrasting a grand New York concert hall with a faded English seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is a seaside town in Kent; the question mark flags that the definition is just one example of where such a person might top the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is a hugely famous performer, the kind whose name heads the programme at a prestigious venue.

clue.text: Rhythm bashed out with right hand? You shouldn't trust it

indicators.note: out tells us the following letters are to be removed from the word
something bashed is knocked out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right
H is the abbreviation for hand

explanation.surface: A drummer's rhythm thumped out with the right hand proves unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R and H out of RHYTHM, leaving YTHM, then rearrange those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a widely held but false belief, so it is a story you should not rely on.

clue.text: Contemporary desk producing rigorous observation on love in Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so the two are joined in that order
in places the joined pieces inside the word for the country

blocks.note: a crit is a critique, a searching critical appraisal
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A modern writing desk somehow yields a strict study of romance in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contemporary' here means of its own period, not modern: the answer is an old French word for a writing desk.
explanation.definitionFit: An écritoire is a writing desk; 'contemporary' hints at its period, the age when such French furniture was in fashion.

clue.text: Grand army spirit

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a host is an army or a great multitude

explanation.surface: A mighty army has a fighting spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a disembodied spirit of a dead person, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Rococo altar chest, one of many in the Vatican (10, two words)

definitions.text: one of many in the Vatican

indicators.note: rococo describes an extravagantly ornate style, so these letters are elaborately rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ornate chest by the altar, one of many treasures held in the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinals wear red hats, and with so many cardinals in Rome the Vatican holds many of these hats.

clue.text: Theatre awards, acceptable within limits

indicators.note: within puts one word inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: on as in 'that's not on', meaning acceptable
ties are bonds or restraints that limit a person

explanation.surface: Theatre prizes given only to work that stays within proper bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tonys are Broadway's annual theatre prizes; Chambers allows this plural spelling of Tony.

clue.text: The old bent over regarding work

blocks.note: as to means concerning or regarding
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Elderly people stooped over their labours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' is not the elderly: it marks the answer as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Astoop is an old adverb meaning in a stooping position, that is, bent forward.

clue.text: With introduction of rule, parent becomes terrifying no longer

indicators.note: introducing something into a word means putting it inside

blocks.note: a familiar word for a father
R is the abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: A father who brings in house rules stops being frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into DAD. 'No longer' does not mean the opposite: it says the word is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Drad is an obsolete form of dread used as an adjective, meaning dreaded or terrible.

clue.text: Fellow receiving relative, Scottish cow?

indicators.note: something receiving another word takes it in, holding it inside

blocks.note: a don is a university fellow
an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: A college man takes in a kinswoman and asks if she is a Highland cow.
explanation.walkthrough: Cow is a verb here, to intimidate, not the farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Daunton is the Scots form of daunt, meaning to subdue or intimidate, just as to cow someone is.

clue.text: Capital piece of origami

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a run of its letters, found inside it

blocks.note: the middle four letters

explanation.surface: A fine example of Japanese paper folding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like praise for the origami, but it means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia.

clue.text: Hinged front of desk writer's standing above, in fact

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
in a down clue standing above means placed first, on top of the next piece
in places the joined pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
first letter of desk
deed means fact, as in 'in deed'

explanation.surface: A desk with a hinged front, with the writer's pen standing on it, indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact' reads as 'indeed', but it splits into the insertion signal and the word that holds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Depended can mean hung down from a support, and a hinged flap hangs from its hinge.

clue.text: CEO's getting frisky – monkeys with English country dance

indicators.note: frisky letters jump about playfully, so they end up rearranged
getting adds the next pieces on after the first

blocks.note: the chief executive's, with its S
a sai is a South American capuchin monkey
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A company boss lets loose, larking about with monkeys at a rural dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An écossaise is a lively country dance, originally thought to be of Scottish origin.

clue.text: Orcadian dwarf in boat rowing … one such

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A small Orkney sprite sits in a rowing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One such' points out that a trow appears in the fragment, and trow is also a dialect word for a kind of boat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orkney and Shetland folklore a trow is a troll or mischievous dwarf-like creature.

clue.text: Prepare for exam and face success (5, two words)

blocks.note: mug is slang for face
up as in being ahead or on top, a success

explanation.surface: Study for a test and confront success.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for studying hard and fast for an exam, much like cramming.

clue.text: Writings I penned I noise abroad, to spread the word?

indicators.note: something penned is shut in, enclosed inside the other word
abroad means widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: MSS is the abbreviation for manuscripts
taken as written
the second I, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer sends their noisy manuscripts overseas to spread their message.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first I is penned inside the writings; the second simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To missionise is to do missionary work, preaching and spreading the gospel.

clue.text: E,g, O. Peterson directed this old player

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptically: what the pianist Oscar Peterson led was ...
second meaning: an archaic word for an actor

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, HIS TRIO: the Oscar Peterson Trio was the jazz pianist's famous group. 'Player' is a stage player, not a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrio is an old word, from Latin, for a stage actor.

clue.text: Runny miel's spread around – it results in various recipients getting the same

definitions.text: it results in various recipients getting the same

indicators.note: something runny flows and loses its shape, so the letters are rearranged
around suggests the letters are moved about into new places

blocks.note: taken as written, the French for honey
marge is short for margarine, a spread

explanation.surface: Runny honey has been smeared everywhere, and now everyone gets an identical sticky share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb about the honey but is the noun, margarine. Its letters join MIEL in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail merge is a word-processing feature that sends one standard letter to many addressees, each copy personalised.

clue.text: Men gripped by rhythmical music – lancers put it on

indicators.note: something gripped by another is held inside it

blocks.note: ska is a Jamaican style of music with a strong offbeat rhythm
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught up in rhythmic music while cavalrymen get dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A schapska is the flat-topped Polish-style helmet worn by lancers, a headdress they put on.

clue.text: Taste eel? No, oddly like bony fish

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are put into an odd new order

blocks.note: all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone declines to sample eel, finding it strangely like a bony fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' does not ask for odd letters here: every letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Teleostean describes the teleosts, the large group of fish with bony skeletons.

clue.text: One who triumphed in New World parliament

definitions.text: One who triumphed in New World

blocks.clueFragment: One who triumphed in New World
blocks.note: first meaning: Hernán Cortés, the Spanish conquistador of Mexico
second meaning: the legislative assembly of Spain or Portugal

explanation.definitionFit: Cortés conquered the Aztec empire in the Americas, and the Cortes is the Spanish national legislature.

clue.text: Like splotchy art? This chap's is received in display of discretion

indicators.note: a word that is received in another is taken inside it

blocks.note: tact is discretion shown in dealing with others
this chap's means his

explanation.surface: Is this blotchy artwork the man's, shown with discretion?
explanation.definitionFit: Tachisme is an abstract painting style using blobs and splashes of colour; tachist describes it.

clue.text: Page like this is set before those investigating e.g. booklouse

indicators.note: set before means placed in front, so the pieces are joined in this order

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
so means in this way
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A page shown to detectives investigating a book pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A psocid is any insect of the order Psocoptera, which includes the tiny booklouse.

clue.text: Paired cymbals creating a bit of laughter in chart-toppers

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: hits are records at the top of the charts
ha is a single burst of laughter

explanation.surface: Drum cymbals raise a laugh in hit records.
explanation.definitionFit: A hi-hat is a pair of cymbals mounted on a stand and clashed with a foot pedal.

clue.text: You'd find Isis traditionally providing setting for these

definitions.text: You'd find Isis traditionally providing setting for these

indicators.note: the words provide a setting, holding the answer within them

blocks.note: runs from the second letter of the first word into the second word

explanation.surface: The rites of the goddess Isis traditionally featured these instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the sistrum was the rattle shaken in the worship of Isis in ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sistra, plural of sistrum, are metal rattles used in ancient Egyptian worship, especially of Isis.

clue.text: Where notice 'as been posted giving chocolate ingredient?

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptically: a pin-hole, with the H dropped as the apostrophe in ''as' hints
second meaning: a meal of parched maize used in some chocolate drinks

explanation.walkthrough: Pinned-up notices leave a pin-hole; said with a dropped H, as ''as' signals, that is pin 'ole.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinole is parched cornmeal, mixed with sugar and spices, and used in making chocolate drinks.

clue.text: It's describing what you should do about spore clusters, itchy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: PC, politically correct, is the done thing
sori, plural of sorus, are clusters of spore cases on ferns

explanation.surface: Advice on handling fungal spores that leave you itching.
explanation.definitionFit: Psoric means relating to psora, an itching skin disease such as scabies.

clue.text: An old dog I spot – it's seen in larder often (10, two words)

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a rach is an old word for a scent hound
taken as written
to soil is to spot or stain

explanation.surface: Someone notices an old dog sniffing about the pantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachis oil is groundnut or peanut oil, a common cooking oil kept in many kitchen cupboards.

clue.text: Latin above entrance in kirk? It could be

definitions.text: Latin above entrance in kirk? It could be

indicators.note: in a down clue above means placed first, so the pieces are joined in that order

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Latin
ingo is a Scots word for an entrance; a kirk is a Scottish church

explanation.surface: A Latin inscription carved over a Scottish church door.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the Latin over the church door is itself a language, and 'it could be' says Latin is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is a casual word for a language, and Latin is one.

clue.text: One in five have optical fault missing peripheral characters

blocks.note: to squint is to have eyes that do not align

clue.text: Boy marries? It may have meant holy obligations

definitions.text: It may have meant holy obligations

blocks.note: a son is a boy
ties as in ties the knot, marries

explanation.surface: A young man weds, perhaps out of sacred duty.

clue.text: Turned well before middle of turn

indicators.note: before means placed in front, so the pieces are joined in this order

the central two letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' is milk gone off, not rotated.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that has turned has gone sour, so both words describe food that has spoiled.

taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Mad career taking in starter's signal? One witnesses that

blocks.note: taken as written
go is what a starter calls to begin a race
